properties.name: Göbekli Tepe
properties.description: Published Taş Tepeler site on the Germuş limestone, and a UNESCO World Heritage property. A known validation site for this project, not a discovery. The years are a filter bracket for the published occupation, not a new chronology.
properties.notes: Official listing coordinates. 30 m terrain cannot resolve individual enclosures or pillars.

properties.name: Karahan Tepe
properties.description: Published Taş Tepeler excavation on the Tektek plateau. A known validation site, not a discovery. Years are a filter bracket.
properties.notes: Public encyclopedia coordinates of a published excavation.

properties.name: Sayburç
properties.description: Published Pre-Pottery Neolithic site on the Şanlıurfa plateau. Years are a broad filter bracket, not a dated building sequence.
properties.notes: Public encyclopedia coordinates. The pin is not a surveyed plan.

properties.name: Harbetsuvan Tepesi
properties.description: Published Pre-Pottery Neolithic site on the Tektek plateau. Years are a broad filter bracket.
properties.notes: Public encyclopedia coordinates. The pin is not a surveyed plan.

properties.name: Nevalı Çori
properties.description: Published Pre-Pottery Neolithic site. It now lies under the Atatürk reservoir. Years are a filter bracket for the PPNB settlement.
properties.notes: The published location is submerged. The pin is not a place on dry ground, and the surface here is the reservoir, not the excavated settlement.

properties.name: Harran
properties.description: Historic town on the Harran plain. Kept with the original six published points as a landscape landmark, not as a Taş Tepeler site. The date bracket is why it also appears in later periods.
properties.notes: Not a Neolithic discovery and not part of the Taş Tepeler group.

properties.name: Edessa
properties.description: City of the County of Edessa, taken in 1098 and lost to Zengi in 1144. The pin is the published coordinate of the historic city, now Şanlıurfa.
properties.notes: City coordinate, not a traced circuit of the crusader walls.

properties.name: Antioch
properties.description: City of the Principality of Antioch after the siege of 1098, held until the Mamluk conquest of 1268. The pin is the published coordinate of Antakya.
properties.notes: City coordinate, not a traced circuit of the walls.

properties.name: Nicaea
properties.description: The First Crusade besieged Nicaea in 1097. The city then returned to Byzantine control. The pin is the published coordinate of İznik.
properties.notes: Marks the published city, not a reconstructed siege line.

properties.name: Dorylaeum
properties.description: First Crusade battle near ancient Dorylaeum. The Wikipedia coordinate sits on the ancient city, not on a surveyed battlefield polygon.
properties.notes: Battle area. Drawn as an open ring. Do not treat this as the exact spot of the fighting.

properties.name: Constantinople
properties.description: The Fourth Crusade sacked Constantinople in 1204. The pin is the published coordinate of the historic city.
properties.notes: City coordinate. It does not mark a single building of the 1204 sack.

properties.name: Turbessel
properties.description: Crusader stronghold of the County of Edessa. English Wikipedia identifies Turbessel and Tilbaşar with Gündoğan, Oğuzeli. The pin uses that page's coordinate.
properties.notes: Published identification of the site with this village and mound. Not a traced castle plan.

properties.name: Ravendel
properties.description: Crusader castle of the County of Edessa. Wikidata's castle item places it in the Polateli area. Another Wikidata item sits about 12 km to the southwest, so this pin is approximate.
properties.notes: Drawn as an open ring. Q11904675 gives a different published point. Not a confirmed wall line.

properties.name: Rumkale
properties.description: Castle on the Euphrates, held in the Edessa period and later an Armenian catholicos seat, taken by the Mamluks in 1292. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate.
properties.notes: Published site coordinate of the standing ruins.

properties.name: Birecik
properties.period: Euphrates crossing of the County of Edessa
properties.description: Euphrates town associated with the County of Edessa. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of the modern town, not a traced castle.
properties.notes: Town coordinate for a historic crossing and settlement.

properties.name: Samosata
properties.description: Ancient Samosata, held for a time by the counts of Edessa. The published site is now under the Atatürk reservoir. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of Samsat.
properties.notes: The historic site is submerged. This is the published location, not a place on dry ground.

properties.name: Marash
properties.period: Frankish and Armenian rule, late 11th–12th century
properties.description: City on the edge of the County of Edessa, taken in the First Crusade period and later contested. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of Kahramanmaraş.
properties.notes: City coordinate, not a traced citadel plan.

properties.name: Baghras
properties.period: Templar castle above the Syrian Gates
properties.description: Castle guarding the Belen pass north of Antioch, held for long stretches by the Templars. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate.
properties.notes: Published coordinate of the castle site.

properties.name: Tarsus
properties.description: Cilician city taken during the First Crusade and later part of the Armenian kingdom of Cilicia. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of Tarsus.
properties.notes: City coordinate. The date bracket covers the crusader and Cilician connection, not every earlier century of the city.

properties.name: Mamistra
properties.description: Ancient Mopsuestia, called Mamistra in crusader sources, on the road between Tarsus and Antioch. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate.
properties.notes: Published site coordinate.

properties.name: Adana
properties.description: Cilician city contested in the First Crusade and later under the Armenian kingdom. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of Adana.
properties.notes: Modern city coordinate. Not a traced medieval wall.

properties.name: Saleph crossing
properties.description: Frederick Barbarossa drowned in the Saleph, the Göksu, on 10 June 1190 while the German crusade was near Silifke. The ford is not precisely mapped. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of Silifke.
properties.notes: Open ring. This is the nearby town, not a surveyed drowning spot.

properties.name: Smyrna
properties.description: The Smyrniote crusade held a harbor castle at Smyrna from 1344 until Timur took it in 1402. That castle does not survive as a plan. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of historic Smyrna.
properties.notes: Open ring. City coordinate, not the vanished harbor castle's footprint.

properties.name: Bodrum Castle
properties.description: Hospitaller castle of St Peter at Bodrum, begun after the loss of Smyrna and held until 1522. Later than the 12th-century crusader states. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of the standing castle.
properties.notes: Included because it is the Hospitaller successor to Smyrna. The date is 15th century, not 1096–1200.

properties.name: Çatalhöyük
properties.description: Neolithic settlement on the Konya plain. UNESCO dates eighteen occupation levels on the eastern mound to 7400–6200 BCE. The western mound continues into the Chalcolithic, to about 5200 BCE. A known published site, not a discovery.
properties.notes: Listing coordinates N37 40 0 E32 49 41. The years used for the period filter are the eastern mound.

properties.name: Aşıklı Höyük
properties.description: Aceramic Neolithic mound on the Melendiz, southeast of Aksaray. Wikipedia records first settlement around 8200 BCE. The end year is a filter bracket for that occupation, not a new chronology.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate of the mound, about 1 km south of Kızılkaya.

properties.name: Boncuklu Höyük
properties.description: Neolithic village mound about 9 km from Çatalhöyük. Wikipedia dates the occupation to about 8300–7800 BCE.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. The pin is the mound, not a building plan.

properties.name: Çayönü
properties.description: Pre-Pottery Neolithic settlement northwest of Diyarbakır. Wikipedia dates its prosperity to about 8630–6800 BCE.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate of the published excavation.

properties.name: Hallan Çemi
properties.description: Protoneolithic site in southeastern Anatolia. Wikipedia says it was founded about 9500 BCE and is more than 11,000 years old. The start year is a filter bracket so the Neolithic chip can include that founding date.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. Round houses and early pigs are published; this pin is not a trench plan.

properties.name: Körtik Tepe
properties.description: Early settled site on the Batman Çayı. Wikipedia dates occupation from about 10400 BCE to abandonment around 9250 BCE.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. The site is published and excavated, not a discovery.

properties.name: Hacılar
properties.description: Early settlement mound 23 km south of Burdur. Wikipedia dates the earliest stage to 7040 BCE and notes later abandonment and reoccupation. The end year is a filter bracket for the Neolithic chip, not a claim that occupation stopped in 6000 BCE.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate of the mound.

properties.name: Can Hasan
properties.description: Mound group northeast of Karaman. Wikipedia attributes Can Hasan 1, the coordinate used here, to the Chalcolithic, and Can Hasan 3 to the Neolithic. The start year is a filter bracket so the Neolithic chip includes the group. It is not a claim that Can Hasan 1 began in 6000 BCE.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate of Can Hasan 1. Can Hasan 3 is not given a separate pin.

properties.name: Hattusa
properties.description: Hittite capital at Boğazkale. The UNESCO listing describes the city and its second-millennium influence. These years are a filter bracket for the Hittite capital, not a full occupation history.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. The UNESCO listing 377 page did not publish a point.

properties.name: Troy
properties.description: The mound of Hisarlık, with a Bronze Age citadel and lower town and later Greek and Roman Ilion. The filter years cover the Bronze Age sequence. Later occupation is real and is not what this chip is selecting.
properties.notes: Listing coordinates N39 57 23.184 E26 14 20.4.

properties.name: Kültepe
properties.description: Bronze Age city and Assyrian trading quarter on the central plateau. Wikipedia places the settlement broadly in 3300–1200 BCE and the famous tablets in the early second millennium. The pin is only resolved to about a kilometre.
properties.notes: Open ring. The Wikipedia latitude is given only to 0.01 degree.

properties.name: Alacahöyük
properties.description: Mound northeast of Hattusa with Early Bronze Age tombs and a later Hittite settlement. The years are a filter bracket for those published phases.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate of the mound.

properties.name: Arslantepe
properties.period: Late Chalcolithic palace and Early Bronze Age
properties.description: Tell in the Malatya plain. UNESCO highlights the Late Chalcolithic palace, about 3400–3100 BCE, and an Early Bronze Age royal tomb. Later Hittite levels exist and are not the filter bracket used here.
properties.notes: Listing coordinates N38 22 55.92 E38 21 39.93.

properties.name: Karkemish
properties.description: Ancient capital on the Turkish–Syrian border, held at times by Mitanni, the Hittites, and the Neo-Assyrian empire. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of the site. The years are a filter bracket, not a dynastic list.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. Part of the site lies on the Syrian side of the modern border.

properties.name: Gordion
properties.description: Phrygian capital southwest of Ankara. UNESCO describes the Early Phrygian citadel and the Midas Mound. The years are a filter bracket for that Iron Age capital.
properties.notes: Listing coordinates N39 38 36 E31 59 10. A Wikipedia point sits about a kilometre away; this pin uses the listing.

properties.name: Sardis
properties.description: Capital of Lydia, near Sart in Manisa. The filter years run to the Persian takeover in 546 BCE. The city continued through the Hellenistic and Byzantine periods.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. UNESCO inscribed Sardis in 2025; that listing page was not used for the point.

properties.name: Ephesus
properties.description: Ionian and Roman harbour city at modern Selçuk, with earlier settlement nearby. The filter years cover the Hellenistic city through the early Christian centuries. The UNESCO listing page did not publish a point.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate of the ancient city. UNESCO listing 1018.

properties.name: Pergamon
properties.description: Attalid capital and later Roman provincial capital above Bergama. Wikipedia dates the kingdom to 281–133 BCE. The end year keeps the Roman and late antique city inside the Classical chip.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate of the acropolis. The UNESCO listing 1457 page did not publish a point.

properties.name: Aphrodisias
properties.description: Carian city near Geyre, with a temple of Aphrodite from the 3rd century BCE and a Roman civic centre. The years are a filter bracket for that city.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. The UNESCO listing 1519 page did not publish a point.

properties.name: Zeugma
properties.description: Hellenistic and Roman city of Commagene at a Euphrates crossing in Gaziantep province. Part of the site was later flooded by the Birecik reservoir. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of the city.
properties.notes: Wikipedia coordinate. Not a mosaic-by-mosaic plan.

properties.name: Mount Nemrut
properties.description: The hierothesion of Antiochus I of Commagene on Nemrut Dağı, a tumulus with colossal statues. The years are a filter bracket around that 1st-century BCE monument.
properties.notes: Listing coordinates N37 58 50.86 E38 44 27.54.

properties.name: Göreme
properties.description: Town in the Cappadocian valleys, a centre of Byzantine rock-cut churches and hermitages. The pin is the Wikipedia coordinate of the town, not one church. The years are a filter bracket for that Byzantine use.
properties.notes: Town coordinate inside the Göreme National Park landscape. UNESCO listing 357 did not publish a point on the page checked.

properties.name: Ani
properties.description: Ruined medieval city in Kars province, capital of the Bagratuni kingdom in 961–1045 and occupied earlier. The end year matches the Classical and Byzantine chip. Later occupation continued after 1095.
properties.notes: Listing coordinates N40 30 0 E43 34 0.
